Appearance:
NIRAV C BHATT(7420) for the Applicant(s) No. 2,3 RAHUL S SHAH(9701) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR.DIPAK B PATEL(3744) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR SOAHAM JOSHI, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================

sentences.text: The present application is filed by the applicants under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for quashment of the impugned FIR being C.R. No.11191030200014 of 2020 registered with the Mahila Police Station (West), Ahmedabad City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 114 of the Indian Penal Code as well as charge-sheet and the Criminal Case No.39194 of 2020 pending before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Ahmedabad.

2. The brief facts of the prosecution case are that after about two months from the marriage, the applicants were harassing the complainant - wife for small things; and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14218/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined that they pressurised the complainant for conceiving the child,; and that they demanded dowry and thereby mentally tortured the complainant.
Hence, the impugned complaint.

sentences.text: 3. Heard learned advocates.
4.1 Learned advocate for the applicants has submitted that there is no prima facie case made out against the applicants.
He has submitted that the allegations made in the present FIR are general in nature and it is filed with an oblique motive to exert pressure on the applicants.
He has further submitted that applicant no.1 is the husband applicant nos.2 and 3 are the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the complainant.
He has further submitted that the husband and wife were residing separately from the in-laws since long.
He has submitted that there were quarrels between the husband and wife which are normal in nature, however, the in-laws are falsely dragged into the litigation.
He has submitted that this is a case of over implication and the entire family is dragged by the complainant.

He has submitted that this is nothing but the abuse of process of law by the complainant and this Court may exercise the powers in favour of the applicants under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
He has submitted that this application may be allowed.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14218/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined 4.2

In support of his submissions, he has relied upon the following decisions :
(i) 2018 (0) AIJEL - SC 63030 - Anand Kumar Mohatta versus State (Government of NCT of Delhi) Department of Homes (ii) 2009 (0) AIJEL - SC 47730 - Neelua Chopra versus Bharti 5.1

sentences.text: Per contra, learned advocate for complainant has submitted that there is a prima facie case against the applicants.
He has submitted that all the applicants have played vital role in torturing the complainant mentally and physically.
He has submitted that the in-laws were torturing for conceiving the baby to the complainant and thereby harassed the complainant.
He has submitted that many a time, the in-laws have tried to give fuel to the quarrels between husband and wife and thereby they have tortured mentally to the complainant.
He has submitted that the applicants have demanded dowry from the complainant also.
He has submitted that this is not a fit case where this Court should exercise the powers under Section 482 of the Code in favour of the applicants.
He has submitted that this application may be dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14218/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined 5.2

In support of his submissions, he has relied upon the following decisions :
(i) 2011 (0) AIJEL - SC 224799 - Naynaben W/o Jagdishbhai Hashmukhbhai Maisuria versus State of Gujarat (ii) 2003 (0) AIJEL - SC 30928 - Superintendent of Police (C.B.I.) versus Tapan Kr.Singh 6.

He has submitted that looking to the complaint itself, prima facie case is made out against the applicants.

He, therefore,
submitted that there is no case made out to interfere by this Court by exercising the powers under Section 482 of the Code as it is a case for trial.
He has submitted that this application may be rejected.
7. I have heard rival contentions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties.
I have also perused the documents available on record.

Considering the submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties and also considering the documents available on NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14218/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined record, the following factors are weighed with this Court for consideration of this application.

In this matter, investigation is over and charge-sheet is filed, which culminated into Criminal Case No.39194 of 2020 before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Ahmedabad and the trial is already commenced.  Prima facie case is made out against the applicants as the applicants pressurised the complainant to conceive the baby against the wish of the complainant.

When the complainant and her husband got separated for few months, at the time, the in-laws have given mental tortured by pressuring the complainant about more facilities to be provided to the sister-in-law.
Prima facie, it seems that the in-laws gave mental torture to the complainant.
The complainant tried to resolve the dispute amicably, but the applicants did not respond to it.

Any Indian lady would have done waited for some time to resolve the matrimonial dispute rather than take the aid of criminal complaint against the in-laws, which the complainant has done in the present case.  The complainant has, on 30.12.2019, gave a detailed written complaint to the concerned police officer about the same.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14218/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined
This is not a fit case where this Court should exercise the powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 in favour of the applicants.

8. In view of the settled position of law and after considering the facts stated in the FIR and circumstances of the present case, it transpires that the fruitful purpose would be served if such further proceedings are allowed to be continued.
Let the applicants be faced the trial.
When prima facie ingredients of offence is made out in the complaint, the complaint cannot be quashed, as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court time and again.
Even otherwise, this Court has very limited powers under Section 482 of the Code to quash the complaint.
This application, therefore, needs to be dismissed and is dismissed.
Notice is discharged.
Interim relief stands vacated.
